purpose: Apply only conservative, evidence-backed preserve/review guards before calibration. This file never authorizes unattended semantic deletion.

evidence.interpretation: The cards support only exact preserve/block safeguards. They do not authorize a positive semantic deletion rule.

autocut_policy.scope: no automatic semantic deletion; machine-assisted draft remains subject to the current run's representative human calibration and final human listening

rules.evidence: Project preference: a standalone acknowledgement can carry interpersonal meaning; preserve it rather than infer that it is a filler.
A weak spoken connector inside an incomplete/unknown clause must not be deleted from text shape alone.
Human feedback identified these exact ASR/token-boundary false positives. The rule is intentionally exact rather than a generic lexical guess.
A short Latin fragment joined to adjacent Latin text is more safely treated as an ASR word-boundary error than a removable hesitation.
The same repeated text can be a correction, emphasis, or a real stutter. Without an acoustic/temporal stutter signature it is not low-risk.
Long pauses and semantic/audio events require A/B or semantic review; they can never enter unattended automatic deletion.

rollback: Choose a different frozen policy file for a future run; never rewrite a run that already contains this policy SHA.
